name: Springy UI motion
oneLiner: Motion design for the windows and menus a game already draws: panels open with an elastic pop, slide or unfold and close faster than they open, list rows stagger in, the selection highlight glides between rows on a damped spring and the chosen row lifts, numbers roll to their new value and a backdrop dim fades. The game keeps drawing every window at its final rect; the module only wraps those draw calls, never reads or delays input, and runs on its own step clock so frozen screenshots and autoplay stay deterministic.
fits: turn-based RPG battle (command menus, spell lists, target cursors)
top-down adventure / RPG (dialogue, shop, bag, pause)
roguelike and deck-builder (reward and shop screens)
any game with windows, menus, toasts or counters
notFor: games whose UI is DOM / HTML rather than canvas (use CSS transitions there)
diegetic in-world UI that must stay locked to a 3D surface
competitive games where any motion near the HUD is unwanted (use reduced: on, or skip)

needs: a fixed update step to advance the module clock (update(dt), also run by ?t= fast-forward)
each window's existing draw code, with a stable id and its final rect in screen units
optional: the cursor index of each menu, rects of its rows, numbers worth rolling
optional: where game logic opens / closes a window (open(id) / close(id)) for exact mid-animation frozen frames
provides: open / close animation of any window the game draws (pop, slide, unfold), close played from a copy so game state closes at once
row stagger and selected-row lift (row(), rowOffset())
a spring-gliding highlight or pointer rect (glide()) and rolling numbers (count())
backdrop dim and soft window shadows
debug() / stats() / state() for tests (open and close timings); never an input gate

assets: module/springy-ui.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_SpringyUI): analytic spring open curve, exact damped-spring glides and lifts, ease-in close played from a device-pixel copy of the window, row stagger, rolling counters, backdrop dim and soft shadows (colour through GameDNA_Skin palette.ink, built-in pixel16 ink)

module.skin: optional: skins/skin-api.js + a skin before it (only the dim / shadow colour)
